text: Do I recommend this, yes or no? Nothing like an oversimplifying, binary choice. I'm voting "No" at the moment, even though I've had fun with it so far. It all depends on what kind of game you're looking for, and how sensitive you are to the price. And how much it updates. Cities: Skylines this ain't, nor is it really a close sibling to the old Impressions games in terms of complexity. Kingdoms and Castles is really much more basic so far. In all, this title needs quite a bit of work, as of July 2017 -- both game balancing and content expansion. It seemed pretty clear of bugs, except for some of the possible deep-seated issues others have mentioned with how well food is distributed. It's frustrating to see your people starving when there's plenty of food lying around. I get the feeling that it maybe should have waited a month or two to be released into Early Access. Even then, it remains to be seen if the update schedule is often and substantial enough.

title: Kingdoms and Castles
text: It's a cute little city builder, and better than what you would expect for only ten dollars, but you run out of content pretty fast. This isn't the kind of thing you're likely to rack up a three digit playtime on, unless the devs release a lot of new stuff for it. It works like any other city builder: you choose your difficulty, generate a random map, set down your first building, and then get to work harvesting resources for expansion. Grow crops, mine stone, build defenses, and fend off progressively more difficult barbarian waves. The only mechanic which is unique to Kingdoms and Castles is: every map is an island, so all of your enemies either sail in by boat or fly. The game is fun, and I'm sure I'll play it again from time to time but, like I said, there is very little content. There are no scenarios, no campaigns, no win conditions, no alternative maps or factions, and only two kinds of enemies; Vikings and dragons. Later on, Vikings will bring ogres with them. The game is exceedingly easy, even on the hardest difficulty, and you'll see and build everything in the first couple of hours. So, once you build your first city, there is nothing left to do, except the same thing again on a nearly identical map. The devs are still adding content, and they just released another update before I purchased my copy. Their site says they have another on the way, also free. If they keep that up for a couple of years, this game could turn into quite a bargain, but for now it's just a cute little 3D builder that is fun for about 5 hours. If you want to shoot down dragons over your rooftops for a bit, go for it.

title: Kung Fury: Street Rage
text: For $3.29, you could do worse. Kung Fury is an excellent little movie and this game does it a lot of justice. It plays exactly like the awesome stick figure brawler 'One Finger Death Punch', in that the game only runs on two buttons. Enemies will approach from the left and the right, and you press the corresponding buttons to attack. There are several enemies, which take anywhere from one hit up to five hits to defeat, with a couple of them teleporting from side to side. The game throws them at you in different groups so you're always on your toes. There are two modes to this game, the first one being story. This involves you fighting waves of enemies as each of the games characters in four chapters, with a special boss fight at the end of each chapter where you actually get to move around normally. Each of the battles is different and escalates in difficulty with the boss adapting new moves each time. The story mode also features short dialogue scenes containing the actual voice actors from the flim, which is enjoyable but there isn't as much dialogue as there could've been. Endless Mode is the second one on offer, and is basically just what it says; an endless wave of enemies for you to fight against until you die, fighting for a high score all the while. Depending on how much you enjoy the game will determine your mileage on this. What is different from the aforementioned title this borrows from, is the fact that each character is different. **You have KUNG FURY of course, who plays rather ordinary with some flashy kung-fu moves, and three health. No fancy mechanics to him oddly enough. **Then you have BARBARIANNA, who attacks normally with her axe and blasts everything on one side with her gatling gun every fifth hit, and only two health for some reason. **Next up is HACKERMAN, who has to attack or 'hack' four times to charge up his attack, at which point he can actually destroy every enemy on the screen with one hit each as long as you keep attacking to keep it charged. **Lastly is TRICERACOP, who fights similarily to Kung Fury but with guns, and in the process actually shifts backwards on each attack so you can get all the enemies on one side or the other, and he has five health altogether. Each one of these characters plays differently enough to keep the game interesting. For the cost of the game you can get your money's worth. So get this game, go hack and beat up some Nazis and have a nostalgia filled good time.

title: Kung Fury: Street Rage
text: Edit: Free update invalidates any gripes I talk about in this review. I wholeheartedly recommend purchase of this game, the devs listened and expanded the gameplay and it is now SO worth the price. My review marks this game as recommended, If you have not watched Kung Fury, go check it out. Now, about this game... I know if I had seen this in an arcade I probably would have dumped 2$ into it and not been able to take the cabinet home. Having said that, quick list of pros and cons. Pros - Based on Kung Fury. - Supports Laser Unicorns. - Reasonably priced. - Easy to learn. - Good retro style graphics/music. Cons - No reach indicator. (No indicator at all when/if enemies are within range of attack) - Multiplier based scoring, with punishing drops in multiplier for misses and taking damage. at its price point and given that it supports Laser Unicorns, I do recommend it to anyone who really enjoyed the movie and would like to support the creators.

title: LEGO® MARVEL's Avengers
text: 4 Hours into Marvel Avengers, I still can't confidently say whether or not it's a recommended purchase. I don't think this is anything more than DLC that could of been attached to the previous Marvel Lego game. Batman 3 had the Arrow, Man of Steel and Dark Knight DLC and that is what they should of done with this instead of a single full price release. The open world is very much identical, theres a lot of level reuse and all characters have been ported over, though if anything they've been made worse. The combat has been tweaked and not for the better, a lot of hit or miss attacks occur and some characters feel too slow during fighting especially Cap who suffers most. The Thor and Loki fight during the first Avengers section is a tough slog, using button mashing that recycles the animation over and over as you mash the buttons on screen, this happens a lot. It's hard to tell during these sequences if it's actually doing anything or it's stuck on loop. The inclusion of the one button for mutiple uses is frustrating, if your using an xbox controller 'B' can be used as double team attack, fire extinguishing, targeting and building all at the same time. Leading to some deaths that never should of occured, while you frantically try to get the character to do the right action. Cap's fire extinguishing is much worse than the last game, having now to do a two button weird jump animation to put them out rather than hold a button for Cap to place his shield on the ground. The 'B' button finsihing moves are just the end of the combo from the previous game, made as a finishing move. If you played the last game as i have, it doesn't really make any sense as it breaks the flow of the combo and looks janky on animation. Graphically it's not very different from Lego Batman 3 or its predecessor, not a bad thing because there's not much more you can do to a lego game to make it look great anyways. Audio dialogue is taken from the films and honestly i wish they hadn't bothered. It sounds out of place and a lot of the times, poor. The dubbing of effects they've tried to use to make it fit in actually make them stand out. There was a lot of hints to the MCU and characters straight from the movies in the last Marvel Lego, there really was no real need to base an entire game around these two Avengers movies. Maybe it would of been worth the money if it was MCU based and we got to play levels from all MCU films but that's not the case. This really is high priced DLC, unfortunately falling the wrong side of worth the money. If you like Lego games this will keep you entertained, it sucks to be harsh on it but after 4 hours and having 100% the last one, it really doesn't stand up on its own well.

title: LEGO® MARVEL's Avengers
text: The characters alone are worth getting the game. I love the detail in the characters for this and other super hero lego games. Mannhatten is mostly the same, but you can also go to about 8 smaller areas like Tony's house in Malibu and Asgard. You play levels from these movies: Avengers, Avengers Age of Ultron, 1 level with some Captain America, Iron Man 3, Thor 2, and Captain America Winter Soldier. The 2 Avengers movies have about 6 levels. The other movies have 1 level each and no cutscenes. The Hulk vs Hulkbuster level is just some crappy button mashing, which is the only way you fight Hulk. I enjoyed the Avengers movies levels anyway, and defeating Ultron was pretty cool. Tony Stark has about 15 suits including Hulkbuster. Spiderman, Fantastic 4, Xmen, and Guardians of the Galaxy are not in this game. They are in the Marvel Super Heroes game. Instead you get alot more characters. Theres even a T-rex. Combat is more difficult, and you will often die from getting shot because you cant always defend against multiple enemies from different angles. Doing an instant kill attack gets annoying after a while because it takes about 4 seconds. You collect over 200 gold bricks. The reward for collecting them all is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥, tiny stud fountain that is made of regular bricks and not gold ones. Im sick of getting almost nothing for the gold bricks. I hate that. There are no "fun or silly" red bricks. I enjoy having fun making characters tiny or something overpowered, but you just get studs x# or item detector bricks.

title: LEGO® MARVEL's Avengers
text: LEGO Marvel Super Heroes was good, but a lot of people felt kinda lost because it was based on the comic universe, and not the cinematic universe. LEGO Avengers is not only based on "Age of Ultron" (as the cover or even the game's icon will sugest), it covers "The Avengers", "Age of Ultron", "Captain America - The First Avenger", "Captain America - Winter Soldier", "Iron Man 3", and "Thor - The Dark World". The cutscenes recreates the most iconic moments of those movies in LEGO style, and they did a pretty good job with that. Also, the game has audio clips from the movies, that means you can hear Chris Evans, Robert Downing Jr, Chris Hermsworth, etc. This is a great feature for the kids. Gameplay wise, this is the first LEGO game that introduced some new features, like co-op actions, some special finishers, and all the characters actually feel really diferent from each other. Puzzles are the same as always, but at least you have some variation on the fighting parts. Music was taken straight out of the movies, so is great. Unfortunely, the dialogues are very low, and every time your character does an special action, it says some one-liner from the movies, and this gets old...fast. Despite this few things, game is great as all the LEGO ones, and is perfect for kids that only know about the Marvel movies. As always, you have good humor, and a lot of replay value. I still think LEGO Batman 3 is the perfect LEGO game, but this is the best you'll get with Marvel characters. Also, there is future DLC planned to adapt "Ant-Man" and the upcoming "Captain America - Civil War", so there is more content coming. If you are not into Marvel, you might wanna wait some time until a sale, but if you are a Marvel fan, or have kids that most likely love the movies, you should buy this game right now, the effort they put into this game deserves your money.

title: LOST PLANET® 3
text: An intresting game with a pretty decent story line imo. At first I didnt like the game, it seemed like a poor console port, with invisible walls stopping you from accessing certain areas, for eg. a 40ft mech unable to advance past a 1ft step. After awhile though you tend to forgive this poor design and just enjoy the game for what it is..... and that is a pretty decent third person game with plenty of well hidden collectables and exploring to do. I do wish they would have sped the movement up a little although you do have a fast travel option to teleport across map. The graphics are pretty at times and make for some great screenshots, I cant really complain about that department. The achievements are simple to aquire although the collectables can take some finding... a guide will help you alot with this. The multiplayer is ok, survival being one of my favorite game modes although as far as I could tell theres no ingame voice or chat whatsoever making gaming with randoms very hard to enjoy. If youre looking to 100% itll take you 25-30 hrs for the sp and 15-17 for mp. Lots of boosting-grinding needed in mp for the 100% sphere achievement. With all said and done the game was pretty enjoyable.......... buy in a sale and youre onto a winner  7/10

text: A very underrated game, a better deadspace then deadspace 3 at times and a bug free experience for me. Great graphics with a decent (but far from original) scifi story. Since I was dying for some good ol SF this can scratch the itch.

title: LOST PLANET® 3
text: Fantastic atmosphere unlike any other game (I'm a winter person) But the levels are both recycled and repetitive, the music could be better as it tries to force a spooked attitude on you when it's not really scary at all. Controlling the mech is HELLA FUN!
